The pet's colours are CHOSEN, per face set. Five roles — panel, eye, mouth, text, control — live in each set's JSON, so a set is a palette as well as a geometry. This card is generated from those files.

It never follows the phone's theme. The pet is a picture of hardware, not a surface of the app; light and dark are a phone setting and the pet is not the phone. It stays what its set says it is in both.

The ratios are a floor AND a ceiling, and both are load-bearing. Eyes and mouth take WCAG's 3:1 for non-text graphics, the spoken line takes 4.5:1 as text, and the generator refuses a set that misses either — the pet has to be readable across a room, which is further away than the monitor a palette gets picked on. The talk button is the ceiling: it must be findable (1.1:1) and must not compete with the face (4.5:1), because a dark button on a pale panel reads as a hole punched in the pet.

A pure black panel is still worth preferring where a set can take one — unlit AMOLED pixels cost no battery, and the pet runs about 22 h on a 1300 mAh cell. A pale panel lights the whole display and its cost has not been measured.

The placeholder debt is paid. PET_COLOR_EYE and PET_COLOR_TEXT were #00E5FF and #FF4081, taken from filler text in an early draft and in no scheme at all. They are gone, and so is the shape of the problem: colour is not two #defines any more.
